name: Iwokrama Forest
blurb: Guiana Shield rainforest where jaguars, caimans and harpy eagles rule.

tip.title: Remove the tapirs
tip.text: Tapirs eat and spread the seeds of many rainforest plants and feed jaguars and caimans. Set South American tapir to -100% and watch the predators and the forest.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Lowland rainforest turns tropical sunlight into leaves, flowers and fruit, the base of every food chain here.

nodes.name: Rainfall
nodes.desc: Heavy rain keeps the lowland tropical forest of the Guiana Shield green and feeds the rivers that cross the reserve.

nodes.name: Seasonal river flooding
nodes.desc: The Essequibo, Siparuni and Burro-Burro rivers bound and cross the reserve. Rising water spreads into low forest and swamp.

nodes.name: Sandy, nutrient-poor soils
nodes.desc: Some forest here grows on pure white sand, where nutrients are scarce and recycled quickly from fallen leaves and wood.

nodes.name: Fungi and bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves, wood and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Wallaba
nodes.desc: A legume tree of northern South America, also called bootlace tree, that can grow even in pure white sand. Its timber resists decay.

nodes.name: Pepper plant
nodes.desc: A forest understory shrub of the pepper genus. Its fruit is a favourite of Carollia fruit bats.

nodes.name: Cashew-nut tree
nodes.desc: A leguminous tree recorded in the reserve area, common in wet and swampy lowland forest.

nodes.name: Seba's short-tailed bat
nodes.desc: The best-recorded mammal around the reserve. Prefers Piper fruit but also eats other fruit, nectar, pollen and insects.

nodes.name: Leafcutter ant
nodes.desc: Cuts leaves and carries them to the nest to grow the fungus it feeds on. Ranges from Mexico to Bolivia, including the Amazon basin.

nodes.name: Red-rumped agouti
nodes.desc: A rodent that eats mostly seeds, fruit pulp, leaves and roots, and disperses the seeds of some trees by carrying them off.

nodes.name: Guyanan red howler
nodes.desc: A howler monkey native to Guyana and neighbouring countries, living in the forest canopy.

nodes.name: South American tapir
nodes.desc: A browser of leaves, shoots, fruit and aquatic plants that eats and spreads the seeds of many rainforest plants.

nodes.name: Striped forest whiptail
nodes.desc: A fast ground lizard of Amazonian and Guianan forests. It is recorded as prey of the fer-de-lance.

nodes.name: Fer-de-lance
nodes.desc: A venomous pit viper of lowland forest. GloBI records it eating the lizard Kentropyx calcarata.

nodes.name: Amazon tree boa
nodes.desc: Eats a wide range of prey, including frogs, lizards, birds and mammals such as bats. GloBI records it eating a sac-winged bat.

nodes.name: Piranha
nodes.desc: Omnivorous river fish whose diet varies widely: fish and other animals, but also fruit, seeds and leaves. They often scavenge.

nodes.name: Arapaima
nodes.desc: Giant air-breathing fish of the Amazon and Essequibo basins that eats fish, crustaceans, fruit, seeds and insects.

nodes.name: Giant otter
nodes.desc: Hunts mostly fish, especially characins and catfish, in clear rivers of the Guianas and Amazon. Its numbers reflect river health.

nodes.name: Black vulture
nodes.desc: Feeds mainly on carrion, often finding it by sight or by following Cathartes vultures. Among the most recorded birds near the reserve.

nodes.name: Harpy eagle
nodes.desc: Canopy hunter whose prey is mostly tree-dwelling mammals; at nests in Guyana monkeys formed a large share of prey remains.

nodes.name: Jaguar
nodes.desc: Top cat of the Americas, found in Guyana's forests and riverbanks. Takes capybara, peccaries, caiman and other prey as available.

nodes.name: Black caiman
nodes.desc: Largest predator of the Amazon basin, living in rivers and swamps of southern Guyana. Eats fish including piranhas, and mammals.
